title: NUMA Memory Imbalance Per Node
exclusions: Measures only the sustained spread in raw `MemUsed/MemTotal` occupancy among regular-memory NUMA nodes exposed through `/sys/devices/system/node/node*/meminfo`. It does not estimate per-node `MemAvailable`, distinguish reclaimable cache from unreclaimable demand, measure allocation fallback, remote-memory access, latency, bandwidth, page migration, huge-page placement, cgroup or process ownership, or prove application impact or root cause. It does not cover hosts with fewer than two qualified memory nodes, detect an entirely silent host without a separate inventory-backed freshness control, change NUMA policy, or provide security or regulatory assurance. The base report labels active exact-host-and-high-node exceptions but does not discard their rows.
evidence: When deployed, retain the `linux_numa_node_memory_imbalance` saved-report definition, the alert-only derivative and scheduler history, raw `linux:numa_node_meminfo` events for the evaluated ten complete minutes, the effective scripted-input and source-type configuration, collector file hash, same-time node `meminfo` and `numastat -m` comparisons, threshold approval, exception-lookup revision, and exported rows containing `_time`, `host`, `numa_node`, `lowest_used_nodes`, `mem_total_kb`, `mem_free_kb`, `mem_used_kb`, `avg_used_pct`, `host_low_used_pct`, `host_high_used_pct`, `imbalance_spread_pct_points`, `sample_count`, `observed_node_count`, `expected_node_count`, and `disposition`. These artifacts show collection and rule behavior; this documentation review did not produce runtime evidence or establish performance impact.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated index, create eight one-minute buckets ending before dispatch, with one valid `event_version=1 collector=node_meminfo_v1 event_type=node_sample collection_status=ok` event per bucket for each of two nodes on `host=numa-positive`. Set `expected_node_count=2`. For node 0 use `mem_total_kb=1000000 mem_free_kb=200000 mem_used_kb=800000`; for node 1 use `mem_total_kb=2000000 mem_free_kb=800000 mem_used_kb=1200000`. Run the SPL with the isolated index substituted. Expect exactly one row for node 0 with `avg_used_pct=80`, `host_low_used_pct=60`, `host_high_used_pct=80`, `imbalance_spread_pct_points=20`, `sample_count=8`, and `disposition=investigate`, proving both inclusive threshold boundaries and capacity normalization. An unexpired exact `host=numa-positive,numa_node=0` lookup row must retain the base-report row as `approved_test`; the alert derivative ending in `| where disposition="investigate"` must return zero rows.
controlTest.negativeScenario: In separate complete windows, create two-node fixtures with eight valid samples per node. Fixture A uses 80 percent and 60.1 percent occupancy and must return zero rows because the spread is 19.9 percentage points. Fixture B uses 79.9 percent and 49.9 percent and must return zero rows because the high node is below 80 percent despite a 30-point spread. Fixture C has the positive values but only seven samples for node 1; fixture D adds any `event_type=collector_error collection_status=error` event for the host. Both must return zero rows because node coverage or collector health is incomplete. Also verify that a `mem_used_kb` value unequal to `mem_total_kb-mem_free_kb` is rejected rather than coerced.

dataSources: A locally managed Splunk Universal Forwarder scripted input examines every `/sys/devices/system/node/node*/meminfo` during each 60-second poll and emits one compact key-value event per node with nonzero `MemTotal` to the deployment-selected `index=os` and local convention `sourcetype=linux:numa_node_meminfo`. The successful contract is `event_version=1`, `collector=node_meminfo_v1`, `event_type=node_sample`, `collection_status=ok`, `numa_node`, `expected_node_count`, and integer `mem_total_kb`, `mem_free_kb`, and `mem_used_kb`; all three memory values preserve the kernel file's kB unit. `_time`, `host`, and `source` are Splunk metadata. Classified collector-error events share the source type. The custom source type and fields are not supplied by Splunk or the optional Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux.
app: Splunk Universal Forwarder native scripted input packaged in a locally maintained app such as `TA_linux_numa_node_meminfo`. No Splunkbase app, premium Splunk app, modular input, HEC token, or `Splunk_TA_nix` input is required for this custom event contract.
spl:
index=os sourcetype="linux:numa_node_meminfo" earliest=-10m@m latest=@m
| eventstats count(eval(event_type="collector_error" OR collection_status="error")) as collector_error_events by host
| fields _time host event_version collector event_type collection_status collector_error_events numa_node expected_node_count mem_total_kb mem_free_kb mem_used_kb
| eval event_time=_time, event_version=tonumber(event_version), numa_node=tonumber(numa_node), expected_node_count=tonumber(expected_node_count), mem_total_kb=tonumber(mem_total_kb), mem_free_kb=tonumber(mem_free_kb), mem_used_kb=tonumber(mem_used_kb)
| where collector_error_events=0 AND event_version=1 AND collector="node_meminfo_v1" AND event_type="node_sample" AND collection_status="ok" AND isnotnull(host) AND numa_node>=0 AND expected_node_count>=2 AND mem_total_kb>0 AND mem_free_kb>=0 AND mem_free_kb<=mem_total_kb AND mem_used_kb>=0 AND mem_used_kb<=mem_total_kb AND mem_used_kb=mem_total_kb-mem_free_kb
| bin _time span=1m
| stats latest(event_time) as sample_time latest(mem_total_kb) as mem_total_kb latest(mem_free_kb) as mem_free_kb latest(mem_used_kb) as mem_used_kb dc(expected_node_count) as declared_node_counts latest(expected_node_count) as expected_node_count by host numa_node _time
| where declared_node_counts=1
| eval used_pct=100*mem_used_kb/mem_total_kb
| stats avg(used_pct) as avg_used_pct latest(mem_total_kb) as mem_total_kb latest(mem_free_kb) as mem_free_kb latest(mem_used_kb) as mem_used_kb latest(sample_time) as sample_time count as sample_count by host numa_node expected_node_count
| where sample_count>=8
| eval avg_used_pct=round(avg_used_pct,2)
| eventstats dc(numa_node) as observed_node_count min(avg_used_pct) as host_low_used_pct max(avg_used_pct) as host_high_used_pct max(sample_time) as _time by host expected_node_count
| eval low_node_marker=if(avg_used_pct=host_low_used_pct,tostring(numa_node),null())
| eventstats values(low_node_marker) as lowest_used_nodes by host expected_node_count
| eval imbalance_spread_pct_points=round(host_high_used_pct-host_low_used_pct,2), sample_age_seconds=now()-sample_time
| where observed_node_count=expected_node_count AND host_high_used_pct>=80 AND imbalance_spread_pct_points>=20 AND avg_used_pct=host_high_used_pct
| lookup linux_numa_memory_exceptions.csv host numa_node OUTPUT valid_until_epoch change_id reason
| eval valid_until_epoch=tonumber(valid_until_epoch), disposition=if(isnotnull(change_id) AND valid_until_epoch>=now(),"approved_test","investigate")
| table _time sample_time host numa_node lowest_used_nodes mem_total_kb mem_free_kb mem_used_kb avg_used_pct host_low_used_pct host_high_used_pct imbalance_spread_pct_points sample_count observed_node_count expected_node_count sample_age_seconds disposition change_id reason
| sort 0 -imbalance_spread_pct_points -avg_used_pct host numa_node
description: Reports the most occupied regular-memory NUMA node when all expected nodes have at least eight valid samples in the last ten complete minutes, the high node averages at least 80 percent raw `MemUsed/MemTotal` occupancy, and its spread from the least occupied node is at least 20 percentage points. It normalizes unequal node capacities and preserves source kB values, node coverage, sample count, and exception disposition for triage.
value: A persistently fuller NUMA node can be an early clue to asymmetric workload placement, memory policy, or node-level demand even while another node retains headroom. Capacity-normalized comparison helps Linux teams decide where to investigate without the divide-by-zero behavior and unequal-capacity bias of an absolute-free-memory ratio; explicit completeness and persistence guards reduce pages caused by missing polls or brief allocation bursts.
implementation: Deploy the documented read-only `node_meminfo_v1` scripted collector at 60-second intervals, preserve the kernel's kB unit, and verify every node event against the same poll's sysfs file and `numastat -m`. Schedule the report every five minutes over ten complete minutes and start with the local policy of eight samples per expected node, high-node average occupancy of at least 80 percent, and a spread of at least 20 percentage points. Baseline by hardware and workload class before paging, monitor host freshness separately, and notify only on `disposition=investigate`.
visualization: Use a host-by-node heatmap of `avg_used_pct` from all valid node samples, with labeled 80-percent occupancy and 20-percentage-point spread policies. Pair it with a latest-results table containing high and low node identities, source kB fields, sample and node counts, age, spread, disposition, and change ID; add 24-hour per-node occupancy lines and a separate inventory-backed collector-error/stale-host panel. Label the metric `raw MemUsed occupancy`, not available memory, pressure, remote access, or latency, and drill down to source events plus the NUMA investigation runbook.
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable. `linux:numa_node_meminfo` is a local operational metric contract with no claimed CIM data-model mapping; the primary search must validate and aggregate raw events.

knownFalsePositives:
A returned row is a real difference in the kernel's raw node occupancy snapshots. "False positive" here means the difference is expected, reclaimable, or not operationally harmful—not that the collector invented a value.

1. **Intentionally asymmetric workload placement** — A database, JVM, virtual machine, or analytics worker may be bound to CPUs and memory on one node while another node is reserved for a different service. Confirm the service configuration, `numactl --show` or approved launch policy, effective cpuset CPU and memory nodes, and `/proc/<pid>/numa_maps`. If the placement is designed and tested, use a threshold or exact-node exception owned by that workload rather than suppressing every host of the model.

2. **File cache or reclaimable slab concentrated on one node** — Kernel `MemUsed` is `MemTotal-MemFree`; it is not per-node `MemAvailable` and includes memory that may be reclaimable. Compare `numastat -m`, the node file's `Active(file)`, `Inactive(file)`, `FilePages`, and `SReclaimable`, plus host-wide pressure and reclaim signals. Keep the result as an occupancy observation, but do not page it as proven shortage when cache explains the spread and service objectives remain healthy.

3. **Approved startup, failover, restore, or batch window** — First-touch allocation during a database start, VM failover, in-memory cache warm-up, backup, or model load can create a sustained but expected ten-minute difference. Match the exact host, high node, service, and UTC window to the change or job record; retain the base-report row and mute only the bounded notification.

4. **Explicit interleave, preferred-node, membind, or cpuset policy** — NUMA policy can deliberately shape node occupancy, and CPU migration can make current placement differ from a simple socket expectation. Inspect the policy and allowed memory nodes before proposing rebinding. A stable imbalance under a reviewed policy may need a workload-class threshold; it is not evidence that Linux ignored the policy.

5. **Asymmetric or changing hardware topology** — Memory hotplug, a memoryless node, firmware configuration, or an intentionally unequal-capacity platform can alter node membership. The percentage calculation handles unequal capacities, but an `expected_node_count` change or collector error invalidates comparison for that window. Reconcile `/sys/devices/system/node/online`, `has_normal_memory`, each node's `MemTotal`, and the hardware inventory before re-enabling notification.

6. **Collector duplication or delayed ingestion** — Two active scripted stanzas, old field contracts, or delayed events can distort bucket selection and sample counts. Compare `_raw`, `source`, collector version, and `splunk btool inputs list --debug`; remove the duplicate or repair routing, then rerun both controls. Do not tune the occupancy threshold around a collection defect.

**Suppression contract:** create `linux_numa_memory_exceptions.csv` with headers `host,numa_node,valid_until_epoch,change_id,reason`. Use the exact Splunk host and numeric high-node ID, UTC epoch seconds, no wildcards, one accountable change ID, and a bounded expiry. The base SPL classifies but never removes an active exception. Create the notification search from the base report and append `| where disposition="investigate"`; lookup editing must be restricted and revisions retained.
hardware: Linux bare-metal hosts or guests that expose at least two regular-memory NUMA nodes through `/sys/devices/system/node/node*/meminfo`. Hypervisor vNUMA, memory hotplug, memoryless nodes, and unequal node capacities require topology qualification; the percentage calculation normalizes capacity but does not validate topology quality.
mitreAttack: N/A (operational Linux NUMA capacity monitoring; no adversary behavior is asserted)
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and measurement boundary

Assign a Linux performance/capacity owner and a Splunk content owner. Use Linux hosts that expose at least two nodes with nonzero `MemTotal` under `/sys/devices/system/node/node*/meminfo`. The forwarder service account needs read and traverse access to those sysfs paths and its ordinary outbound forwarding route; test access as that account before deployment and do not grant root or memory-policy capabilities merely to read sysfs. The search owner needs access to the selected event index plus permission to create a report, alert, and lookup. `index=os`, the app name, source type, collector name, and normalized fields are local conventions, so change inputs, searches, controls, and role grants together if the deployment uses other names.

Linux documents each node `meminfo` as a per-node view of memory distribution and utilization. Current kernel source emits `MemTotal`, `MemFree`, and `MemUsed` in kB and computes `MemUsed` as total minus free. This use case deliberately calls `100*MemUsed/MemTotal` raw occupancy. It is not the host-wide `MemAvailable` estimate and does not subtract file cache or reclaimable slab. The upstream `numastat -m` view reads the same node files and converts values for display in MB; it is a human cross-check, not the collector's parse target. Default `numastat` hit/miss counters answer a different question and are covered separately by UC-1.1.25.

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Create `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/TA_linux_numa_node_meminfo/bin/collect_node_meminfo` from `scriptExample`, owned by the deployment account and executable by the forwarder service. The first pass counts readable node files whose parsed `MemTotal` is greater than zero. Fewer than two qualified nodes cannot produce a cross-node comparison, so the script emits a classified error instead of a fake balanced state. The second pass emits one successful sample for each qualified node, a `not_applicable` inventory record for a zero-total node, or a classified error for unreadable, missing, nonnumeric, or internally inconsistent values. It never replaces a failed value with zero.

The script preserves kB exactly and requires `MemUsed=MemTotal-MemFree`. It does not parse `numastat -m` table columns, whose presentation and MB rounding are unsuitable as a machine contract. It also does not emit `host`; Splunk input metadata owns that identity. Configure the local input:

```ini
[script://$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/TA_linux_numa_node_meminfo/bin/collect_node_meminfo]
disabled = 0
interval = 60
index = os
sourcetype = linux:numa_node_meminfo
```

Leave `source` at the script-path default for provenance. Splunk documents that scripted-input stdout is indexed and stderr goes to `splunkd.log`; this script keeps classified states on stdout. At 60 seconds, a continuously connected host with two regular-memory nodes produces about 2,880 successful node events per day, plus inventory or error events when applicable. The interval is measured around script execution rather than a guarantee of wall-clock-perfect polls.

On the parsing tier configure `[linux:numa_node_meminfo]` with `SHOULD_LINEMERGE = false` and `DATETIME_CONFIG = CURRENT`; on the search tier set `KV_MODE = auto`. The lines have no embedded event time, so `_time` is collection/ingestion time. Place each property on the correct tier for the deployment topology. No CIM acceleration, HEC endpoint, API credential, inbound port, `numactl` package, or Splunkbase add-on is required.

Run the script as the forwarder user and compare every successful line immediately with its named node file. Verify one line per qualified node, integer kB fields, exact subtraction, stable `event_version` and collector name, and a correct `expected_node_count`. Then run `splunk btool inputs list --debug` to confirm one winning stanza, path, interval, index, and source type. Do not proceed while two stanzas collect the same files.

### Pre-alert field and node qualification

Search the last 15 minutes and inspect `_raw` with all required fields. Each continuously collected node should have roughly one event per minute; normal scheduler and ingestion skew are why the alert accepts eight rather than demanding ten. For every successful event, `mem_total_kb` must be positive, free and used must be between zero and total, and used must equal total minus free. Compare the set and count of node IDs with `/sys/devices/system/node/online` and `has_normal_memory`, then explain any online memoryless node or hotplug state in the host inventory.

At the same instant, run `numastat -m` if the numactl package is already approved. Expect its per-node total, free, and used display to correspond after kB-to-MB conversion and display rounding; do not demand character-for-character equality from samples taken at different times. Also retain the raw sysfs comparison, because it is the collector's actual source. `numastat` without `-m` displays allocation statistics, not this occupancy snapshot.

Create a separate inventory-backed health rule. It must report expected hosts with no recent `node_sample` or `collector_error`, hosts with any collector error, unexpected node-count changes, and nodes with fewer than two polls in a three-minute allowance. The primary report cannot discover a completely silent host. Never coalesce silence to zero occupancy or describe an error-suppressed host as balanced.

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Save the primary SPL as `linux_numa_node_memory_imbalance` and schedule it every five minutes, with trigger condition result count greater than zero. Its embedded `earliest=-10m@m latest=@m` evaluates ten complete minute buckets and excludes the still-arriving current minute. `eventstats` first counts classified errors across each host; any such error suppresses that host from this capacity rule and leaves collector health to the separate control.

**Understanding this SPL:** The numeric and consistency checks enforce the documented event contract. `bin` plus `stats latest(...)` selects one newest sample per host, node, and minute, preventing a retry or duplicate line from overweighting the average. The next `stats` computes mean raw occupancy independently for every node and requires at least eight represented minute buckets. `eventstats` then derives the number of qualified nodes and the host minimum and maximum. `observed_node_count=expected_node_count` prevents a missing node from becoming a valid comparison. Only the highest-occupancy node or tied nodes remain.

The inclusive starting policy requires `host_high_used_pct>=80` and a high-minus-low spread of at least 20 percentage points. Percentages normalize unequal node capacities; unlike the former `max_free/min_free` ratio, the calculation neither compares unlike absolute capacities nor divides by a free value that can approach zero. Eight samples, 80 percent, 20 points, the ten-minute window, and the five-minute schedule are catalogue policies—not Linux, numactl, or Splunk defaults. Baseline by hardware model, kernel line, vNUMA topology, memory policy, and workload class. Record threshold changes with an owner, rationale, effective date, and repeated boundary tests.

Create `linux_numa_memory_exceptions.csv` exactly as specified in `knownFalsePositives`. Keep the base report's two dispositions. Derive `linux_numa_node_memory_imbalance_alert`, append `| where disposition="investigate"`, and route it to the Linux capacity owner. Key notification throttling by `host,numa_node` for one schedule interval; do not use an indefinite throttle that conceals a persistent condition.

## Step 3 — Validate logic and host behavior

Run both `controlTest` scenarios in a temporary index with fixed timestamps in complete minute buckets. The positive fixture intentionally uses different node totals: 800,000 of 1,000,000 kB is 80 percent, while 1,200,000 of 2,000,000 kB is 60 percent. The expected 20-point spread proves inclusive boundaries and percentage normalization. Verify absent/expired lookup data yields `investigate`, while an active exact-node entry yields `approved_test` in the report and no row in the alert derivative.

Run each negative guard separately: 19.9 points, high occupancy below 80, seven samples on one node, a collector-error event, inconsistent arithmetic, only one expected node, and a changed expected count. Preserve exact fixture events, search bounds, job IDs, output or zero-output, and lookup revision. A later runtime reviewer should repeat tests on supported deployment versions; this editorial review establishes documented semantics and static arithmetic only.

For host acceptance, capture the script line, indexed event, and source file from the same poll. Compare `numastat -m` after unit conversion, then run an owner-approved representative workload long enough to observe normal placement without exhausting memory. If investigating a named process, use `/proc/<pid>/numa_maps`, its effective cpuset memory nodes, and approved launch policy. Correlate node occupancy with host pressure/reclaim telemetry and application latency before claiming impact. Do not change binding, migrate pages, drop caches, or stress production memory merely to make the alert fire.

## Step 4 — Operationalize and investigate

Build the heatmap, trend, result, and freshness views described in `visualization`. Restrict report, alert, and exception edits to the platform role; grant service owners read access only to their hosts. Review baselines after kernel, firmware, hypervisor topology, memory hotplug, application placement, or collector changes and on the local capacity-review cadence. Retain suppressed rows so planned asymmetry remains visible.

When a result fires, first verify recency, collector health, node counts, and the raw source values. Determine whether file cache or reclaimable slab explains raw occupancy, then identify workloads active during the exact ten-minute window. Check CPU affinity, effective cpuset CPU/memory sets, NUMA policy, process mappings, service starts, failovers, and batch records. Use allocation-miss telemetry from UC-1.1.25 and application latency as separate corroboration. Treat this result as a placement/capacity lead, not an automatic instruction to rebalance.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot and retain evidence

For no events, run the script as the forwarder account, inspect the sysfs glob and effective stanza with `btool`, verify index routing and forwarder connectivity, and search `splunkd.log` for the exact script path. A single-node guest legitimately emits `fewer_than_two_memory_nodes` and belongs outside this alert inventory. For null fields, inspect `_raw`, the exact source-type spelling, and search-tier `KV_MODE`. For merged lines, fix `SHOULD_LINEMERGE` where parsing occurs. For unexpected error suppression, search `event_type=collector_error` and resolve its specific `error_code`.

If Splunk and `numastat -m` appear different, align sample time and units first: indexed values are integer kB, while numastat displays converted MB with rounding. If `MemUsed` is called available memory or pressure, correct the panel and runbook rather than changing arithmetic. If node counts change, reconcile topology and wait for a fully qualified window. If duplicate per-minute events appear, locate overlapping stanzas by `source` and disable the duplicate. Fix collection and rerun controls before tuning thresholds. Retain the saved-search export, scheduler history, source/result rows, collector hash, effective configuration, host comparisons, test outputs, threshold approval, and expiring exception records under the organization's operational evidence policy.
grandmaExplanation: We compare the memory fill level of each part of a large server. If one part stays much fuller than the others, the team can check whether work was placed unevenly before deciding that anything needs to change.
